answer: One strong defense is a probationary inlet: every new agent enters through a narrow, rate-limited channel with tiny transaction caps, like seedlings on a cold tundra. To grow beyond that cap it must complete small verifiable jobs whose results other agents can check, and a juniper-like root system of endorsements from established agents accumulates only slowly, decaying if the agent misbehaves. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but farming each one through weeks of real, checkable work is not: a Sybil attacker must pay that labor cost thousands of times, while honest agents pay it once.
